title: Today Show host Jenna Bush Hager shares ideal 'next chapter' plans for when she leaves show - NewsBreak
text: NBC morning show host Jenna Bush Hager is ahead of the game when it comes to planning for her future life. On Wednesday, the Today with Jenna & Friends co-host spoke about her ideal plans for her “next chapter” if and when she decides to leave the TV show . “I have this sort of dream — I just think everybody should have chapters in their lives — I have a dream — I don’t know how realistic it is — but when the Jenna & Friends chapter comes to a close…” Jenna explained at the beginning of Wednesday’s show. “Well, why would that ever happen?” her guest co-host Matt Rogers chimed in. READ MORE: Fox News Greg Gutfeld 'confirms' swirling rumors on his co-star Jesse Watters READ MORE: Ed Sheeran reveals the traditional Irish song he wants played at his funeral “Well.. linear television, baby!” Jenna added. “Who knows? But when I’m ready to go to my next chapter, I think it would be so nice to move back to Texas and let my kids — I went to a big public high school — have a different life.” Talk of Jenna’s life outside of Today came amid her and Matt talking about whether they’d be willing to go back to their hometown. Daughter of former President George W. Bush and First Lady Laura Bush, Jenna grew up in Austin, Texas. She admitted on the show she’d be open to coming back to the city to raise her three children with husband Henry Hager. “Isn’t Austin great? I love Austin,” Jenna, who shares daughters Mila, Poppy, and son Hal, with husband Henry, raved. Jenna has already begun attempting to give her kids a taste of her childhood Texas experiences this summer. When talking about the tragic flooding in Kerrville, Texas, Jenna disclosed that she sends her children to Texas camps each summer. Jenna stated on-air that she expressed to her husband after he asked why they sent their brood all the way to Texas for camp that it was “Because of the love that's there,” adding, “Texas camps are institutions.” The TV personality became a correspondent on the Today Show in 2009, and in 2019, she began co-anchoring the show’s fourth hour with Hoda Kotb after Kathie Lee Gifford left. Until January 2025, Jenna and Hoda were the titular anchors of Today with Hoda & Jenna. Since Hoda’s departure, Jenna has been having a rotating chair of celebrity guest co-hosts while she’s searching for a permanent replacement. "We're still searching," Jenna told People in June. "We definitely want somebody permanent at some point just because that's our show, and I think the Today show is such a family."
